correctness.rationale: For any complement to TV, unique lifts normalize by a T-commuting module automorphism to span{e1,Pe1+e2}; the map is well-defined and invertible because the diagonal polynomials have nonzero constants. For r>=1, a quotient of the d-step Krylov column matrix is Hankel H_ij=b_(1+i+j), with 2r-1 independent coefficients. Dwivedi--Grinberg Theorem 1.1 gives q^(2r-2) singular arrays among q^(2r-1), yielding exactly (q-1)q^(4d-5) splitting complements. Equal blocks all split by the free-module basis criterion. Exact normalized enumeration (d=3,4) and separate all-subspace enumeration (d=3 over F2) agree. The theorem covers prime powers via field algebra; tests over prime fields corroborate but are not the proof.

value.rationale: The splitting-space count is a natural operator invariant governing two-vector block Krylov success. The result covers every nilpotent two-block Jordan similarity type at fixed even dimension and all prime-power fields, exhibits surprising complete independence of positive block imbalance, and provides a uniform exact success probability not resolved by the previously displayed degree-restricted formulas. A full infinite family and a structural Hankel explanation—not an isolated small numerical table—support mathematical value.
